messages:
maya: Heads-up 1: Product review needs a single, consolidated tenancy playbook that covers lanes, cross-region fallback, canary gates, and customer SLAs. Want owners + launch gates by next Tues.

sam: Agree. Proposing a micro-DLS (policy primitives) so infra/runtime can evaluate routing decisions at request time. Keep it small: lane, residency, fallback, cost_tier, qcompat.

jana: Customers split into three archetypes in my interviews: Enterprise (pinned region + legal residency), Scaleups (dedicated capacity optional, predictable latency), and Startups (best-effort, cheapest lane). We should map them to lanes with clear contract language.

rolf: Operational input: We cannot enable pinned-region lanes without per-tenant tracing and eviction automation. Add these telemetry gates: per-tenant p50/p95/p99, tail retries, evictions/ooms, autoscale actions, and regional capacity headroom metric. If those are missing, block canary. :warning:

ben: For prioritization, I suggest we score each ask on: customer_impact (0-10), dev_effort (0-10), infra_risk (0-10), legal_compliance_need (0-10). We'll normalise and plot. Can someone own scoring?

maya: Ben take scoring. Sam draft the DSL and sample policy. Rolf enumerate telemetry + runbook tasks. Jana collect contract language examples and 3 customer quotes. Sonja, please check billing attribution and rate-limit implications for lanes. I'll collate.

sam: WIP DSL sketch (YAML-ish):
```
lane: gold
residency: region(us-east-1)
fallback:
  - lane: regional_affinity
  - lane: shared_infra
cost_tier: premium
constraints:
  p99_ms: 200
  quant_compat: true
  kms_required: true
rollout: [feature_flag_canary, ab_test, global_cutover]
```
Notes: runtime must be able to evaluate 'quant_compat' and pick quantized variant.

rolf: I'll add a runbook snippet: if eviction_rate > 0.3% over 10m -> trigger autoscale-policy 'burst' and route new sessions to fallback lane. Also add a telemetry sanity check prior to canary: no missing tenant_labels, KV-cache warming rate > 60% after 5m.

sonja: Billing note: lanes should carry a billing_tag so we can attribute delta costs to customers. Also rate-limit tiers must be explicit per lane to avoid noisy neighbor problems.

jana: Customer quote examples added to the draft doc (enterprise Contract Corp wants "data never leaves EU"; startup BetaApp wants cheapest lane "we pay per successful token only").

ben: I'll create the prioritization matrix doc and add 6 sample asks to score. Suggest we weight customer_impact x2 when scoring.

maya: Deploy-bot - can you scaffold a central doc + branch? Also, Taylor will own slides for the review.

deploy-bot: created doc https://redwood.internal/docs/unified-tenancy-playbook and branch routing/unified-playbook-1799997770

taylor: I'll make a 3-slide deck: TL;DR, lanes + customer mapping, gating matrix. Meeting Thurs 9:30?

maya: Thurs 9:30 works. Please add your section to the doc by EOD Wed. We'll use the prioritization matrix during review to pick PI work.

sonja: One more: track any model-variant compatibility (quantization, f16 vs int8) as that will affect fallback quality and SLOs.

sam: Good call. I'll add a 'quality-degradation' field in the policy spec that the rollout tool can use to compute acceptance thresholds. Example: quality_degradation_pct: 3 (acceptable drop vs baseline during canary).

maya: Perfect. See you at review. Thanks all.
